Bug_Title: Child class methods named for parent class methods should be overrides
Bug_Explanation: When a method in a child class has the same signature as a method in a parent class, it is assumed to be an override. However, that’s not the case when the parent class method is static and the child class method is not.
Seed_Compilation_Fail_Details:

Trigger_Explanation: The bug here is that the method getList in Child is not overriding the method from the Parent class. The Child method is trying to override a static method which is not possible. Also, the return type of the method in Child is different than the Parent method.
Model_Explanation: The described bug is not present in the provided Java code. The method 'getList()' in the Child class is indeed an override of the method in the Parent class. The '@Override' annotation is used to ensure this, and the method in the Child class does return a new ArrayList instead of the static list in the Parent class, which is the expected behavior.
